threads.body: This assertion relies on an exact JSON string match, which is brittle (serialization can legitimately change key ordering/formatting across client/library versions). Consider asserting via JSON parsing (compare semantic structure) or using a weaker assertion that still proves 'unsanitized' behavior (e.g., contains the literal value \"test\" and does not contain \"?\").

`try (generator)` is only valid with Java 9+ (try-with-resources on an effectively-final variable). If this module is compiled with Java 8 source/target (common for javaagent code), this will not compile. Fix by declaring the resource in the try header (e.g., `try (JsonGenerator generator = ...) { ... }`) or by creating a separate variable and declaring that one in the try-with-resources header.

`try (generator)` is a Java 9+ try-with-resources feature (resource variable in the try header). If this module is compiled with Java 8 source/target (common for javaagent code), it will not compile. Use a Java 8-compatible try-with-resources form (e.g., declare the resource inside the try header) while preserving the current conditional creation logic.

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: This module sets `minJavaVersionSupported` to Java 11. The `try (generator)` resource-variable form is supported from Java 9, so it is valid for every supported runtime. The current form also keeps the conditional generator creation clear.

Upsides: Keeping the code avoids an unnecessary rewrite and preserves the direct ownership of the selected generator.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: The new configuration’s description doesn’t mention the key safety implication that disabling sanitization will record query bodies verbatim and may capture sensitive/PII data (this warning exists in the PR description/README). Please add that caution to the `metadata.yaml` description as well, since this file is commonly used for generated config docs.
